newsitem.title: USA: VLSI to close wafer plant, take Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: VLSI to close wafer plant, take Q4 charge.

text.p: Custom chip maker VLSI Technology Inc Thursday said it plans to cease production at its San Jose wafer fabrication plant by the end of 1997, a move which will result in 300 job cuts and a fourth quarter charge of between $100 million and $120 million.

In a statement, VLSI said the San Jose plant has been underutilized since the company began shifting to new markets in 1995. VLSI now focuses on providing semiconductor devices for cable and satellite set-top boxes, wireless communications such as cellular phones, networking equipment, computing and secure products.

"These new growth markets require leading edge process technology available at our newer fab located in San Antonio," Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Al Stein said. "Despite the excellent performance of our San Jose fab and its people, the plant no longer supports our business strategies."
The job cuts will take place over the next 12 months.

The company said the decision to shutdown the San Jose plant came only after the company had attempted to increase utilization by marketing the plant as a foundry, and by searching for potential buyers or investors. The company said it plans to continue looking at other options to divest itself of the plant.

The company said it will meet with its customers and align its production schedule with their specific product requirements. The company said the cutbacks will not affect VLSI's other San Jose-based operations, including its corporate headquarters, a technology development group and production test and prototype assembly facilities.
Employees whose positions are eliminated in the shutdown will be given 60 days notice and a competitive severance package, VLSI added.
